MSFT.rationale: Microsoft delivered strong Q3 FY2026 results with 18.3% YoY revenue growth, 40% Azure growth, and a $37B AI revenue run rate (up 123% YoY), all beating consensus. The company's fundamental health is excellent: 67.6% gross margin, 46.3% operating margin, $78.3B cash vs $40.3B debt, and $46.7B quarterly operating cash flow. However, the stock sold off ~5% post-earnings due to the $190B calendar 2026 capex guide (vs ~$154B consensus), with $25B attributed to component price inflation. The commercial RPO grew to $627B but only added $2B sequentially vs $233B in the prior quarter, raising questions about backlog momentum. Valuation is attractive vs its own history: P/E of 29.9x sits near the bottom of the 25.4-42.8x 12-month range, and P/B of 8.65x is well below the 7.3-12.6x range. The stock is down ~24% from its 52-week high of $555.45. Near-term catalysts include the Q4 earnings report (guided $86.7-87.8B revenue) and potential Azure reacceleration, but the massive capex trajectory and OpenAI partnership restructuring introduce uncertainty about long-term returns on invested capital. Google Cloud's 63% growth rate is outpacing Azure's 40%, and the loss of OpenAI exclusivity weakens a key competitive moat. The voluntary buyout program targeting older employees signals cost discipline but also workforce transition risk. Overall, Microsoft remains a high-quality franchise with strong AI positioning, but the capex intensity debate and competitive dynamics cap the upside at a moderate level.

Microsoft stock sinks as AI spending ramps to $190 billion as Q3 earnings top forecasts. Shares fell 5% after company said capex for calendar year 2026 would reach $190 billion

The commercial backlog barely increased sequentially ($2B gain vs. $233B prior quarter), with much of the growth attributed to OpenAI rather than broad-based demand. Azure growth remained flat at 39% constant-currency across three quarters
Google Cloud achieved 63% revenue growth in Q1 2026, significantly outpacing Microsoft Azure (40%) and Amazon AWS (28%)

Microsoft's Azure and other cloud services surged 40%. Annualized revenue from AI altogether now stands at $37 billion, up 123%. Microsoft now has $627 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations, up by $2 billion from the prior quarter.

OpenAI and Microsoft have revised their partnership agreement. While Microsoft remains OpenAI's primary cloud provider, OpenAI can now distribute products across competing cloud providers. Microsoft's exclusive license to OpenAI's models ends, though revenue-sharing continues through 2030.
